bug_functions: lib/rules/indent.js//function that checks indentation of parenthesized values
1.explanation: The regression arises in the parts of indent.js that (1) add indentation for the right-hand side of binary/logical expressions and (2) handle parentheses pairs. The BinaryExpression/LogicalExpression listener is responsible for computing the extra indent for the RHS of `b && (…)`, and the parenthesized-values function determines how tokens inside matching parentheses are offset or collapsed. Both rely on OffsetStorage.setDesiredOffset to record those offsets. Because the new algorithm doesn’t collapse the offset across the wrapping parentheses correctly, it over-indents the JSX. Fixing those two functions (and/or how they invoke setDesiredOffset when parentheses surround a JSXExpr) will restore the expected behavior.

bug_functions: lib/rules/indent.js//<visitor for BinaryExpression and LogicalExpression> ("Adds indentation for the right-hand side of binary/logical expressions")
lib/rules/indent.js//<function checking parenthesized values> ("Checks the indentation of parenthesized values, given a list of tokens in a program")
2.explanation: The mis-indentation stems from the two parts of the new indent.js rule: the visitor for BinaryExpression/LogicalExpression, which computes an offset for the right-hand side, and the logic that handles arbitrary parenthesized expressions. Because the code adds one level of indent for the logical expression and then attempts to re-align the parentheses, it double-counts when the RHS is wrapped in parentheses. Fixing this requires adjusting the binary/logical expression handler so that, when the RHS is a grouped parenthesized expression (especially wrapping a JSX element), it doesn’t add an extra indent beyond what the paren-handler already applies.
2.bug_scenario:
When a JSX element is wrapped in parentheses on the right-hand side of a logical (`&&`) expression inside a JSX return, the new 4.1.0 indent rule mis-computes the expected indentation. In the example: b && (
) each of the lines inside the parens is indented too far (20 spaces instead of 16, or 16 instead of 12), because the rule that handles binary/logical expression indentation doesn’t take the extra grouping parens into account.
